chunks: Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

One who does not hold himself to account every day is not from us. If he has done a good (good) deed, he should seek more of it from Allah and praise Allah for it, and if he has done an evil deed, he should seek forgiveness from Allah for it and turn penitently to Him.
ai.seo_question: What is the daily practice of self-accountability in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes daily self-accountability (muhasabah) as a defining characteristic of the Shia, emphasizing continuous spiritual vigilance. It outlines a dual response to one's actions: expressing gratitude and seeking increase for good deeds, while seeking forgiveness and repentance for faults, thereby integrating the concepts of shukr and istighfar into daily practice.
